name: CA-36
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Ted Lieu holds an overwhelming fundraising edge, roughly $1.8M raised to about $12K for Houston Brignano
District leans Democratic by 21 points on the partisan index
Challenger has almost no cash on hand ($912) and no outside support
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at about 96%
model.rationale: The structural evidence is one-sided: a D+21 incumbent seat, a challenger with essentially no money or outside backing, and markets near 96% Democratic all point to a comfortable Lieu win, with no polls or ratings suggesting any competitive threat.
model.watch: Any late surge in challenger fundraising or Republican outside spending would be the only plausible signal of a closer race, though it would need to be dramatic to matter.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Ted Lieu, the Democratic incumbent, enters the general election as the heavy favorite in a Los Angeles-area district that leans Democratic by roughly twenty-one points. He has raised about $1.8 million and holds nearly $1.2 million on hand, while Republican Houston Brignano has raised about $12,000 with under $1,000 available. Prediction markets give Lieu a roughly 96 percent chance of winning.

No public general-election polls cover the race, so the forecast rests on district fundamentals, the incumbent's financial dominance, and market pricing. All point the same direction: the partisan lean alone nearly guarantees a wide Democratic margin, and the challenger has no visible resources to contest the seat. The realistic question is the size of the victory, not the winner, with a broad double-digit Democratic margin expected.
